chunks: From him, from Safwan ibn Yahya, from Ishaq ibn 'Ammar, who said:

I said to the Virtuous One (peace be upon him): A man points out a commodity to another man and says, 'Buy it, and half of it is mine.' The man buys it and pays from his wealth. He (Imam al-Sadiq, peace be upon him) said: 'He has half the profit.' I said: 'If the price is reduced, will he be affected by the reduction?' He (peace be upon him) said: 'He bears the reduction just as he took from the profit.'

key_terms.اَلْعَبْدُ الصَّالِحُ: The Virtuous One (Title for Imam al-Sadiq, peace be upon him)

ai.seo_question: What are the rules of profit and loss sharing in a silent partnership where one party provides capital and the other provides goods?
ai.summary: In this narration from *Tahdhib al-Ahkam*, Imam al-Sadiq (AS) clarifies the mechanics of *Mudarabah* (profit-sharing partnership), specifically addressing a scenario where one partner contributes expertise or sourcing rather than capital. The Imam establishes the principle of proportional equity: just as the non-capital partner receives half the profit, they must also bear half of any loss or price reduction, ensuring that risk and reward are balanced according to the agreed share. This ruling underscores the Shia juristic emphasis on fairness in commercial contracts, distinguishing it from fixed-fee arrangements.
